change: deploy-gate learns a phase field, so a check can say WHEN it is meaningful, and lib/storefront-fetch.js retries 503 as well as 429
_context: WRITTEN AFTER THE MERGE, and that is the honest order rather than the right
one. PR #735 shipped on a green CI run plus six mutations run by hand, and
those mutations lived in a shell script in a container scratchpad, which dies
with the session. This manifest is how they become something anyone can
re-run. The deploy itself is 0c8de04, already live.
WHY THE CHANGE EXISTED. The FRQ archive gate could not be closed. Its
rederive check runs the generator, every transform in the generator is
find-or-refuse, so once the 2026 scoring note is on the page the check MUST
refuse. It was real evidence before the import and impossible after it, and
the manifest read like a genuine refusal to ship the whole time.
The gate already had the mirror of this hardcoded: live is deferred on a
--pre run because it cannot observe a deploy that has not happened. Nobody
had needed the other direction.
THE MUTATIONS BELOW MUTATE THE GATE ITSELF, which works and is worth stating
because it reads alarming. The gate writes the mutation to disk, runs the
suite as a SEPARATE node process, which therefore loads the mutated file, and
restores it. The gate's own already-loaded module in memory is untouched.
WHY 503 AND NOT 502 OR 504. verify-csa-frq-archive-live walks 142 storefront
requests in one pass. Run three times it lost 7 handles, then 1, then a
different 1, always 503 and never the same handle twice, while every one of
them answered 200 with the expected body when fetched alone. 502 and 504 are
plausibly transient too, and nothing here has observed one. That list earns
entries by measurement rather than by argument.
TWO OF THE ASSERTIONS THESE PIN WERE HOLLOW WHEN FIRST WRITTEN, and the
mutation run is what caught it. The unknown-phase test reused a command
already present in the manifest, so disabling the phase validation left the
DUPLICATE-command rule to refuse it and the assertion passed for the wrong
reason. And an assertion claiming to pin REQUIRED_ONE_OF alone cannot exist:
KINDS has four members, two of which are live and rederive, so a manifest
with neither reaches at most two kinds and MIN_KINDS fires as well. That one
now says so rather than pretending to an isolation that is not available.
THERE IS NO live CHECK, AND THE FIRST DRAFT'S WAS A TIME BOMB. It pinned the
commit sha from /api/health, which is what this repo recommends and is exactly
right for a change that alters what the API serves. This one does not: it is
tooling. So the pin was true for about ten minutes and then three other pull
requests merged, and the manifest could never pass again while reading like a
regression. A gate nobody can pass is worse than no gate.
rederive is the honest kind here, and it does not expire.

checks.name: the gate's own refusals, including every phase path
checks._why: Section 11 is the new one. It pins that a phase:pre check is deferred after the deploy, RUNS before it, that the deferral is named rather than silent, that a misspelled phase is an error rather than a quiet default, and that marking the only outside check pre-only still refuses to ship.

checks.name: the one door, including the retry against a real server
checks._why: Section 7 is the new one, and it had to run the server in its own PROCESS: every caller of storefront-fetch is synchronous, so the Atomics.wait between retry attempts blocks the event loop and an in-process listen() never fires. The first cut died on a null address.

checks.name: a phase:pre check is no longer deferred after the deploy
checks._why: The whole point of the change. Without this the FRQ archive gate goes back to being unclosable.

checks.name: phase:pre is deferred everywhere, so the check never runs at all
checks._why: THE ABUSE THIS FIELD COULD HAVE BECOME. If a phase:pre check is skipped on --pre as well, phase is a way to delete a check rather than to schedule one.
checks.expect_failure: the same check runs and its failure is refused

checks.name: a misspelled phase quietly means the default
checks._why: phase: 'pre-deploy' must be an error. If a typo fell back to 'both', it would silently re-enable a check at the exact moment it cannot pass, which is the same shape of defect as a live check asserting something already true.

checks.name: a deferred check is dropped without being named
checks._why: A gate that quietly drops a check reads like a clean run over work nobody did, which is the failure this whole script exists to prevent.
checks.find: return { ok: problems.length === 0, problems, results, kinds: [...kinds], deferred };
checks.replace: return { ok: problems.length === 0, problems, results, kinds: [...kinds], deferred: [] };

checks.name: 503 drops back out of the retry set
checks._why: The measured failure. Without it, any verifier walking more than a few dozen storefront requests reports a correct site as broken, at random, and a verifier that is red at random gets ignored.

checks.name: the retry stops being narrow and retries everything
checks._why: The narrowness is half the design. A 404 retried three times is still a 404, and waiting on it only makes a red check slower. This is the guard that stops a well-meant widening from costing every missing page the full backoff.
checks.find: for (let i = 1; i < attempts && RETRY_CODES.has(r.code); i += 1) {
checks.replace: for (let i = 1; i < attempts && r.code !== '200'; i += 1) {

checks.name: the retry policy derived from the source and from the behaviour agree
checks._why: Two paths to the same answer sharing no code: a TEXT parse of the RETRY_CODES literal out of lib/storefront-fetch.js, and a behavioural probe of raw() against a local server that answers a code once and then 200, counting how many requests arrive. Each direction of disagreement means something different. In the source but not the behaviour is a set that was widened while the loop cannot act on it, which is what a broken retry looks like while reading perfectly correct. In the behaviour but not the source is something retrying outside RETRY_CODES, so the set is no longer the policy and a reader of the module is being misled. It probes 404, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, so the narrowness is asserted and not only the additions.
checks.expect: the two derivations agree on 2 code(s)
